 Brock Purdy, left, leads the NFC's top team, while Dak Prescott is trying to get the Cowboys back to .500. Ezra Shaw and Stacy Revere / Getty Images 
 By Jon Machota and Vic Tafur Nov. 15, 2026 Updated 8:10 am EST Share article 59 The Athletic has live coverage of all NFL Week 10 action , including Lions vs Patriots in Munich . 
 It may not be the ’80s or ’90s anymore, but it’s still fun when the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers square off.
 San Francisco (7-1) heads to AT&T Stadium with the best record in the NFC. It’s the team’s first trip to Dallas since the wild-card round of the 2021 playoffs, a game best remembered for the clock running out after Dak Prescott scrambled and didn’t have time to spike the ball for one last shot at the end zone.
 Advertisement
 The 49ers have won four straight against the Cowboys, including two in the playoffs. San Francisco has a slim 21-19-1 edge in this rivalry and will debut its latest trade acquisition after landing wide receiver Keenan Allen at the deadline from the Indianapolis Colts at the deadline. Allen should be plenty familiar with the Cowboys’ defense after facing it last week while with the Colts. He had four catches for 26 yards.
 Dallas (4-5) stood pat at the deadline and will have to see if it can go on a second-half run despite owning one of the league’s worst defenses. The Cowboys are near the bottom of the league in points allowed per game (tied for 28th), yards allowed per game (30th), EPA per drive (30th) and total defensive EPA (31st).

 What to watch from the Cowboys
 CeeDee Lamb and Jerry Jones have used the word bittersweet this week to describe the Dallas Cowboys’ season. That’s understandable for Lamb as he’s on pace for 1,700 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns. For Jones, it has clearly been disappointing. The Cowboys owner and general manager believes his team has the personnel to be better than their 4-5 record. Somehow, though, the Cowboys are still completely in the mix to win the NFC East.
 They now face their toughest test of the season, the 49ers (7-1). With how the Cowboys have played the last two weeks against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, handing the 49ers a second loss seems unrealistic.
 During his Friday radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Jones called Sunday, “one of the biggest games we’ve had around here in a long time.” How significant would a win be for Dallas?
 “It would just prove us right,” Lamb said, “(about) how we think of ourselves throughout this building. A lot of people would be shocked, obviously, because of the record and things that have happened leading up to this game. But for us, we know we haven’t played our best game, and we’ve just got to go out there and do that.”
 Prediction: 49ers 27, Cowboys 17 — Jon Machota, Cowboys beat writer

 What to watch from the 49ers
 The 49ers use more pre-snap motion than any other team in the league, and the Cowboys are the worst at defending it. So Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker hopes his team is not “chasing the rabbit all day.”
 The 49ers will lean on their 1-2 running punch of Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black while MVP candidate Brock Purdy welcomes Deebo Samuel (back from a hamstring injury) and Keenan Allen to a passing game that once missed its top five receivers.
 The game might come down to the wire, though, as the San Francisco defense doesn’t have a sack in the last two games and its top two cornerbacks are banged up.
 Prediction: 49ers 27, Cowboys 24 — Vic Tafur, 49ers beat writer
